rules.sentence: As there is no curative therapy for Jacobsen syndrome, prognosis is often determined by the severity of cardiac or hematologic disease.
There is a 20% risk of mortality within the first 2 years of life, often due to complications of cardiac defects or after high-risk cardiothoracic surgery.
The overall life expectancy is largely unknown, although the oldest documented patients have reached 45 years of age.[2]
Patients with Jacobsen syndrome may require surgical and medical interventions throughout their lifetime, reflecting the ongoing need for specialized care and management.

Complications associated with Jacobsen syndrome include developmental and intellectual delays, heart failure from severe cardiac disease, stroke secondary to intracranial hemorrhage, uncontrolled bleeding due to platelet dysfunction or thrombocytopenia, bowel obstruction due to intestinal atresia or malrotation, or skull or skeletal abnormalities.
